notes: contract-check ok=true, violations=[]; not_checked: forbid.behaviors, audited by hand in the notes below.
Diff scope: 14 files, 2188 insertions plus 10 deletions = 2198 lines. Within limits (max_files_changed 18, max_diff_lines 2200) but the line budget is 99.9 percent consumed.

All 14 changed files are in the contract touch list. crates/**, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, rust-toolchain.toml, docs/adr/**, docs/plan/**, docs/PRD.md, docs/bitacora-de-descartes.md and .ai/tasks/** are byte-identical to main, verified with git diff --name-only main...HEAD. No *.db, *.db-wal, *.db-shm, .env* or secret-shaped path appears in the diff.

AC-1 verified: docs/protocolo-ipc-nucleo-sidecar.md covers message format (section 1), Unix domain socket transport (section 2), delivery-confirmation semantics (section 4) and both-endpoint reconnection in all three restart orders (section 5). Version 1.0 dated 2026-07-31, entirely in Spanish, absolute dates only.

Ack semantics are correct: section 4 mandates the durable id_deduplicacion and explicitly forbids a per-connection sequence number; the Confirmacion type carries only that field, and a decoder test rejects a line carrying a secuencia field.

The sqlstore backup operation matches the A-2 contract field for field: order = orden (fixed string respaldar_sqlstore), destino, identificador_de_ronda; acknowledgement = identificador_de_ronda, resultado, ruta_de_la_copia, bytes, motivo. The always-present rule re-expresses the A-2 conditional fields as empty string or zero, preserving the semantics without optional fields on the wire.

No raw transport identifier can cross the port: no message type declares a JID, device-id or phone field, and a test asserts that no field name of any of the six types contains a transport-shaped substring.

The document correctly REFUTES the plan claim at docs/plan/fase-a-3-adaptador-whatsmeow.md lines 96-99 that ChannelAdapter already reserves the session-state field. Verified against crates/hexcell-core/src/canal.rs: the trait declares only send and estado_ventana, and CicloDeVidaSesion only iniciar_emparejamiento and cerrar_sesion. STATUS.md records the correction as pending work for tasks 7 and 10.
No Phase-B-replaces-Phase-A or sidecar-retired wording appears in any changed doc; the protocol doc states the sidecar is a permanent cost per adr-0014.

The Go skeleton is honest: the client is built against store.NoopDevice, Conectar is exposed but called by nothing (not by main.go, not by any test), and there is no net.Dial, net.Listen, pairing or sqlstore code. Imports are stdlib plus whatsmeow only; logging is log/slog with a JSON handler and no new dependency. sidecar/go.mod and go.sum are unchanged and the whatsmeow pin e9a033b24933 is intact.

Tests are behavioural, not filler. Independently re-ran: go build, go vet and go test all clean, 4 packages ok, 24 PASS lines against a floor of 12. Coverage includes round-trip over all six types, twelve malformed-input rejection cases with distinct sentinel errors, field-order and depth-1 assertions on the encoded line, waLog Debugf suppression above threshold, closed log field set with an escaping round-trip, environment defaults and validation, and a doc-structure test that reads the protocol document. cargo fmt, cargo clippy -D warnings and cargo test --workspace re-run green.

Declared deviations judged real and benign: (a) go.mod and go.sum unchanged is correct because whatsmeow was already a direct require, so dropping the blank import needed no manifest change, confirmed by go build passing with an empty go.mod diff; (b) the commit message is a Spanish Conventional Commit with no AI attribution, as CLAUDE.md and the contract require; (c) the dropped canal_test.go case genuinely duplicated assertions that live in registro_test.go, though cutting a test to fit a line budget is worth noting since the budget ended at 2198 of 2200.

MINOR, not blocking, surfaced for the human gate: the plan wording for A-3 task 2 says conexion del websocket, and the skeleton deliberately never connects. This is authorised rather than a gap, because the blueprint declares it deferred by design and the contract forbid explicitly bans opening a real connection, since whatsmeow cannot complete a login without pairing (tasks 4 and 5). The binary therefore starts, logs and waits on SIGTERM without touching the network.

MINOR, for A-3 task 10: the Go decoder inherits encoding/json duplicate-key tolerance where the last value wins, while section 8 does not list a duplicate field as a protocol error. A hand-written Rust parser could resolve duplicates differently, creating a cross-implementation divergence on a malformed peer line. Worth closing in adr-0011 or in the section 8 error list.

MINOR, for A-3 task 3: the stale-socket connect probe of section 2 interacts with the one-active-connection rule. A duplicate sidecar probing a live one would be accepted and would evict the current core connection before the duplicate exits. It self-heals through core retry, but the listener implementation should special-case the probe.

MINOR, verify-command weakness inherited from the contract, not from the implementation: the sixth verify command uses git diff --name-only HEAD, which is vacuous once the work is committed and would pass even if crates or docs/adr had been modified. The intended property was re-checked here with git diff main...HEAD and it holds.

MINOR: the forward reference added to docs/contrato-ipc-respaldo-del-sqlstore.md is a prose note inside section 6 rather than a bare link, but it is explicitly marked non-normative, leaves version 1.0 and the 2026-07-30 date untouched, and keeps adr-0011 as the ADR of record. Within the contract allowance.
summary: Contract satisfied and validation independently reproduced; the protocol doc covers all four aspects, the sidecar never dials, and the Rust workspace is untouched. Approve with notes.
